newsitem.title: LEBANON: SOLIDERE to move to Beirut bourse.
newsitem.headline: SOLIDERE to move to Beirut bourse.

text.p: Lebanon's biggest company SOLIDERE will move its shares from the private Beirut Secondary Market (BSM) to the official Beirut Stock Exchange (BSE) on October 1, market sources said on Monday.
"SOLIDERE has decided to move to the bourse on October 1. It informed the Beirut Secondary Market that the last day of trading there will be September 27," a market source told Reuters.

SOLIDERE has not announced the move but a source close to the company said preparations for it were underway. "If things go as planned, the move will be implemented by the beginning of October," he told Reuters.
The BSM, set up in 1994 under central bank auspices to trade SOLIDERE shares, had been informed, he added.

Market sources said an important reason for the move was a proposal to cross-list SOLIDERE shares on the Kuwait Stock Exchange. The Kuwait bourse set a condition that it would only list shares that were traded on Lebanon's official market, the sources said.
Beirut Stock Exchange officials said the move would inject new life into the market which has been lacklustre since reopening in January after a 13-year gap.
The capitalisation of the Beirut Stock Exchange -- which currently lists only four companies -- is less than $400 million. SOLIDERE would add $2 billion to the market.
However, the move would cast a shadow over the future of the Beirut Secondary Market which currently trades only SOLIDERE shares.
A Beirut dealer said the BSM planned to switch to trading debt and debt-related instruments like convertible bonds, but such instruments were not yet ready.
"It might take some time before the Beirut Secondary Market finds instruments to put on the market to replace SOLIDERE," the dealer said.
A BSM official announced in June that the Lebanese cement company Societe de Ciments Sibline would list its seven-year, 12 percent bonds on the BSM, but they are still under preparation.
The Beirut Stock Exchange currently trades in seven shares of Ciments Libanais, Ciments Blancs, Eternit and Uniceramic.
The official said the transfer "will boost activity on the bourse especially once the 10-for-one share stock-split approved by SOLIDERE shareholders is carried out sometime after the listing".
Stock exchange sources said the market began a two- to three-week testing period last Friday to make sure the official market was technically ready for the SOLIDERE move.
A bourse official said the market was confident. "We have no technical problems as the system is much more sophisticated than that of the Beirut Secondary Market".

SOLIDERE has two types of shares: A shares -- distributed to former holders of property rights in the Beirut central district the company is rebuilding -- and B -- issued in a $650-million subscription in January 1994.
